title: AI presenter
summary: A generated or digital presenter speaking to camera (AI avatar, talking photo, voice over a still, cartoon mascot) for an explainer, onboarding, outreach or a localised version, with consent and AI labels.

notFor.when: the user recorded themselves speaking and wants it cut, captioned or reframed
a dub or translated subtitles of a real recording, with no generated face
generated shots tell a story and nobody speaks to camera
a voice over diagrams, with no presenter on screen

alternatives.when: the user decides to record themselves instead of a generated presenter

qa: The presenter's entity card is user-approved, with likeness and voice consent documented, or not-applicable for an invented or cartoon presenter
Lips match the words on every presenter shot, checked frame by frame at the plosives (p, b, m); a shot that slips is cut to an insert, never shipped
One voice owner per line: the model's native speech or the voiceover, never both
No presenter shot held into drift: face, teeth, hands and eyes stable for the whole shot, and no joint between generated segments left on screen
The AI label for each target platform and the on-screen or end-card disclosure for EU audiences are listed for the user's upload

intake.ask: Who is the presenter: an invented person, a cartoon or mascot, or a real person's face (yours or someone else's)?
intake.why: A real face needs that person's documented consent; a cartoon needs no YouTube label; it decides the entity card and the model.

intake.ask: Whose voice: a stock voice you pick, the video model's own voice, or a clone of a real voice, and whose?
intake.why: A clone needs the owner's consent and ElevenLabs clones only the account holder's own voice; native speech decides which models fit.
intake.default: A stock ElevenLabs voice from a shortlist the user approves by ear

intake.ask: Which languages will the presenter speak?
intake.why: Inspect the selected video.avatar endpoint language policy through models:pick and its exact schema; unsupported languages go voice-first.
intake.default: The language of the request, voice-first

intake.ask: What carries the middle of the film besides the presenter: product screens, diagrams, b-roll?
intake.why: Cutaways hide generation seams and avatar tells; without material for them the presenter must hold longer than models stay stable.
intake.default: Presenter opens and closes; inserts from library blocks or real screens carry the middle

intake.ask: Is it an organic post, a paid ad, or sent one-to-one (sales outreach)?
intake.why: Ads and outreach name a real company and person to strangers: disclosure, consent scope and platform ad rules tighten.
intake.default: Organic post on the named platforms

profiles.note: Realistic presenter: set 'AI use' in Studio; a cartoon presenter is exempt. Length band is a house rule, starting point.
Shorts run up to 3 minutes, square or vertical; the 60 s ceiling is a house rule for a presenter, starting point.
Label AI-generated content showing realistic people; unlabelled posts may be removed or restricted. Length is a house rule.
Meta may require the AI info label on photorealistic video or realistic audio; Reels up to 3 min. Length is a house rule.
LinkedIn takes 3 s to 15 min, ratio 1:2.4 to 2.4:1; the 30-120 s band for onboarding or outreach is a house rule.
EU visitors: disclose a deep fake presenter no later than first exposure (AI Act Art. 50, from 2 Aug 2026). Length is a house rule.

starter.note: One shared grain ties generated presenter shots to inserts; ui-camera-read carries real product screens between presenter shots; TalkingHeadLayout and TalkingHeadVideo in src/templates/talkinghead hold a split or stacked presenter.

variants.title: Talking photo
variants.changes: One supplied still is the key frame; voice first, then a reference-to-video request with the still and the voice as references. Consent for that face is checked before anything is generated.

variants.title: Cartoon or mascot presenter
variants.changes: Stylised character card, no likeness consent (not-applicable) unless drawn from a real person; YouTube exempts animated content from the AI label. May be built in code from library blocks with no generated video at all.

variants.title: The user's own digital twin
variants.changes: The user's own face and voice: likeness and voice consent are documented by the user on the card; a voice clone is made by the user in their own provider account and shared, never by the agent; YouTube treats cloning one's own voice for voice-overs as a minor edit.

variants.title: One presenter in several languages
variants.changes: One approved card and key frame, a reviewed translation per language, a voice per language from generate:voiceover, and a presenter clip per language driven by that voice; word timings per language, never reused.
